# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Remote Access Hardening

Shuts off the WinRM remote shell and disconnects an idle SMB session after fifteen minutes.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | CIS v4 Windows 11 L1 — settings taken from IntuneAdmin, values verified against the settings catalog definitions. |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Remote_Access_Hardening.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Remote_Access_Hardening.json) |

> NOTE before you assign: check that no management script or monitoring tool relies on WinRM. `Enter-PSSession` and `Invoke-Command` keep working — they use the PowerShell endpoint, not the remote shell — but `winrs` and anything built on it no longer do. On a fleet with on-prem management tooling, this is the only policy in this set that can break something you don't see right away. Besides the remote shell, WinRM server management as a whole is now also closed. That is the broader variant: no incoming WinRM connection at all, not just no interactive shell. Check this together with the remote shell setting against whatever management tooling relies on WinRM.
